To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anti-EGFR antibody 7A7 inhibits the metastatic spread of lung cancer cells in mice by a T cell-mediated mechanism of action.
the EGFR-specific mAb 7A7 inhibits metastasis of a murine lung cancer cell line through a mechanism that requires T cell function.
7A7 anti-EGFR antibody is an effective inhibitor of metastatic spread of murine D122 lung carcinoma in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a syngeneic model to study the anti-metatic activity of anti-EGF receptor antibodies and the identification of T cell response as the mechanism of action.

the identification of the mechanisms underlying the anti-metastic effect of anti-EGRF mAbs and the potential role of T cells in this process, which is relevant in the design of new therapeutic approaches for metastatic tumors.
the development of an in vivo syngeneic metastatic model to evaluate the mechanisms associated with anti-EGFR antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anti-EGFR antibodies exert an adjuvant-like effect that enhances T-cell response against the tumor.
the anti-met metastasis activity of 7A6 mAb was mediated, at least in part, by T cells, but not by natural killer cells.
the anti-met metastatic effect of 7A ^{+} mAb is due to the direct anti-tumoral effect of this antibody and the induction of a T cell-mediated anti-metastasis response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

7A7 mAb inhibits the metastatic spread of murine D122 lung carcinoma by a direct anti-prolifterative and pro-apototic effect on tumor metastasis and also by inducing an anti-metastasic T cell immune response.
7A7 mAb is an effective anti-metastasis agent that could be used as an adjuvant in the treatment of metastatic cancer.
anti-metastasis activity of anti-EGR mAb 7A7 is dependent on T cells, and the T cells are the main effector cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anti-EGFR antibodies may have a therapeutic role in cancer metastasis, and this is mediated by the induction of an anti-tumour T cell response.
the anti-met metastatic effect of anti-Egfr mAbs in syngeneic models is T cell dependent.
the T cell response is essential for the therapeutic effect of 7A17 mAb.
